subject: ClearMed: spike in 429s & sustained latency (prod)
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearmed.io>
To: support@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-04-10T15:50:00Z
Subject: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Hi team,

Since ~14:30 PDT we've been seeing a large increase in 429 responses and median latency has jumped from ~120ms to >800ms on our /generate endpoint. Throughput is capped even though our application traffic pattern hasn't changed — we've not changed burst behaviour. This is impacting clinical workflows; some overnight jobs failed and a daytime cohort of requests are timing out.

Attached are a subset of request logs and traces. Can you confirm whether this is a tenant-side policy change or a platform-wide degradation? We rely on the paid plan (dedicated) — this feels like we were routed into a more restrictive window.

Impact: production, multiple customers using ClearMed features blocked.

Please escalate if this is a rate/quota/burst issue.

--
Michael Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearMed Health
Attachment: clearmed_request_logs_20290410.tar.gz (archive)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett, connor_obrien, marcus_lin, vivek_kulkarni, marissa_cole
Date: 2029-04-10T16:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Forwarding ClearMed's report — urgent.

Quick asks:
- Laura: please confirm SLA impact and engage CS playbook.
- Connor & Marcus: can you triage whether this is a rate-limiter/quota/burst misconfiguration or an infra regression? Focus on routing policy for their tenant (dedicated vs hosted fallback).
- Vivek / Marissa: if this is a billing/contract mismatch we may need immediate approval for a temporary quota bump and credit.

I attached the customer's logs from their initial note. I'll patch updates into this thread.

Thanks — Hannah

--
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: clearmed_request_logs_20290410.tar.gz (forwarded)

From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt, laura_bennett, marcus_lin, vivek_kulkarni
Cc: marissa_cole
Date: 2029-04-10T17:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Hannah / team,

I've started a lightweight triage. Initial findings from the customer's logs:
- ClearMed's token usage pattern shows frequent short spikes (bursts) tied to scheduled batch jobs at ~14:25 PDT.
- Our routing logs show that approximately 60% of their traffic in that window was routed to our hosted pool due to a routing rule evaluation (recent rule change on 2029-04-09 that pins a subset of traffic to hosted fallback when dedicated headroom < 20%).
- The hosted pool uses a stricter token-bucket window configuration for that route; given the burst profile the bucket drained and the system began returning 429s, then traffic experienced queue saturation increasing p99 latency.

Hypothesis: a policy change (routing + safety valve) combined with the customer's bursty jobs exhausted burst credits on the hosted variant, causing observed behavior. Not a model or kernel regression.

I am attaching a snapshot of the rate policy we evaluated (rate_policy_snapshot_20290411.json). Next steps: confirm the exact routing criterion hit for this tenant, and determine whether a temporary quota override or adjusting the burst window is lower risk.

--
Connor O'Brien
Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: rate_policy_snapshot_20290411.json

From: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt, connor_obrien, laura_bennett, vivek_kulkarni
Cc: marissa_cole
Date: 2029-04-10T18:00:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Agreed with Connor's hypothesis. Two technical mitigations we can execute immediately:
1) Apply a temporary per-tenant burst-window increase on the hosted route (raise token bucket capacity by 3x for 24 hours) — low-risk and reversible.
2) Pin ClearMed's traffic back to their Dedicated pool while we validate headroom: revert routing rule for their tenant until end of day to prevent further hosted routing.

Operational plan (timeline):
- 18:15 UTC: apply temporary burst-window increase on hosted route for ClearMed (15 min testing window).
- 18:35 UTC: if 430/429s drop and latency improves, start re-pinning traffic to Dedicated pool and continue monitoring for 6 hours.
- 19:00 UTC: update customer and leadership with status.

I will run the first change and monitor traces. Connor, please prepare a rollback play in case we see unintended side effects.

Attachment: mitigation-checklist.txt (internal runbook excerpt)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt, vivek_kulkarni, laura_bennett
Date: 2029-04-10T18:22:00Z
Subject: Re: ClearMed production issue — executive note

Looping in leadership for quick approval. Summary for execs:
- Impact: ClearMed (mid-market healthcare customer, active professional plan with Dedicated capacity) is seeing production 429s and latency spikes affecting patient-facing workflows.
- Cause (prelim): routing + stricter hosted burst quota caused token bucket exhaustion when their batch jobs spiked.
- Ask: approve a 30-day temporary quota/burst bump for CLRM-7892 and a one-time account credit to cover impacted usage; estimated 30k tokens/day incremental.

If approved, we'll apply the bump and issue a notice to procurement to avoid procurement-level pushback. If leadership pushes back, we need to present the trade-offs (downtime vs credit).

--
Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Sales, Redwood Inference

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearmed.io>
Cc: laura_bennett, marissa_cole, connor_obrien, marcus_lin
Date: 2029-04-10T19:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Michael — quick update and next steps.

Thanks for the logs. We identified a routing/quotas interaction that caused your traffic to land on a hosted route with a tighter burst window during a short period of low dedicated headroom. Our immediate actions:
- Temporary burst-window increase applied to the hosted route (18:20 UTC).
- Beginning now we'll re-pin your traffic to your Dedicated pool and continue to monitor for 24 hours.
- We're preparing a one-time quota bump while we validate sustained headroom.

We expect to see 429s drop within the next 15–30 minutes; we'll share monitoring links and a post-incident note when the triage is complete. Apologies for the disruption; we understand this impacts your production workflows.

Can you confirm whether you triggered any ad-hoc batch jobs around 14:20–14:40 PDT so we can correlate?

--
Hannah Schmitt
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachment: mitigation-checklist.txt (internal runbook excerpt)

From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearmed.io>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@clearmed.io, procurement@clearmed.io
Date: 2029-04-12T00:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Production issue — surge in 429s and latency

Hannah / team,

Confirmed — our nightly batch job did run at 14:27 PDT and accounts for the spike you saw. We validated with our users this morning: latency and 429 rate returned to normal after your changes and the re-pin. Thank you for fast triage and the proposed temporary bump — procurement will follow up on the credit discussion and the 30-day bump request.

Please send the post-incident report and the configuration change notes for our audit.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

--
Michael Torres
Head of Platform Engineering, ClearMed Health
